look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Check a simple, heart-shaped to broadly ovate serrated leaf, then the vine's tendril or fruit cluster opposite a leaf. The strongest tie-breaker against Vitis is the cut stem: Ampelopsis has continuous white pith; confirm this rather than relying on berries alone.

project_inclusion.notes: Texas state-level native; target-county certification remains unresolved. Historical Vitis cordata synonym maps here, not a duplicate card.

morphology_keys.habit: Climbing woody vine, often sprawling through shrubs and trees; inspect a complete shoot rather than isolated foliage.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Simple (not compound), alternate, petiolate, heart-shaped to broadly ovate leaves with toothed margins. Tendrils or inflorescences occur opposite leaves.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Small inconspicuous greenish flowers in branched clusters opposite leaves; compare node architecture.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Clusters of small round berries that change color during ripening; berry color alone is unreliable.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Cut a twig to inspect the continuous pale/white pith; compare grape (Vitis) pith and node anatomy.

confused_with: Vitis spp. (grapes; inspect pith and fruit)
comparisons.key_distinctions: A. cordata has simple leaves versus A. arborea's commonly compound leaves; separate simple-leaved Vitis with pith and tendril/cluster structure, not leaf shape alone.
